author: jessica
_note: TESTCASE 01, THE LOAD AT ANOTHER POI. Same four beats and the same prose as duo_delve03, on his
2026-09-24 verdict on that one: the box "should have been at a different POI and then I take it to
that one". So beat 1 is at the SECOND place, and the delivery site is the main place.
His second note, same morning: "the one with the delivery should have people there. It's mainly
caves and natural locations atm." So the delivery site requires LocTypeOE_NonHostile (see _theme),
and the load's own POI takes no theme, because a load can get lost anywhere.
The two item names are Jessica's, 2026-09-24 (see items._items).

2026-10-09: MOVED ONTO THE BEATS KIND (no driver; his "work on the other beats and missions so everything is on this system"). The items block went into the beats it belongs to; every word is unchanged.

place._theme: The DELIVERY site, where people work: LocTypeOE_NonHostile, the engine's own keyword for a site with people on it who are not hostile. Pool 62, measured 2026-09-24. It replaced my first cut (excluding Natural, Cave, Abandoned: pool 121), which approximated people without checking a keyword; his question found this one.
place._civilians: Off: a NonHostile site brings its own people. The carrier's gang is kept, his call: the friendly site gets hit. (2026-10-09: the delve4 'civilians: false' key is gone; a beats Delve with no approach places nobody.)

prose.name: Hauling: Water Reclaimer on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The <Place> is waiting on a reclaimer housing that was signed out to them and never arrived. I should find where the crate stopped.
prose._prose: Rewritten 2026-09-26 against the vanilla style guide (home-office office/projects/bethesda/33-vanilla-quest-text-style.md). This is an ARTIFACT (treasure-map) Delve, his 16:12: 'we'll have both kinds, we've just started on the treasure map (named Artifact in overtime)'. So the title takes the artifact family's shape, Category: thing on <Planet>, which is vanilla's own for this system (slates named 'Report: Abandoned X Shipment') and his base's ('Hauling: Goods Package on <Planet>'). It reads as a plain haul until the core is found missing. Board-kind Delves take the board shape instead. Briefing is the first JOURNAL entry, first person.

beats.journal: I found the housing crate, dropped well short of where it was going. The manifest says a filter core was sent on ahead. I should take the housing to the <Place>.

message.title: Manifest
message.text: The manifest lists two crates for the <Place>: this one, the reclaimer housing, and a filter core sent on ahead. Signed out, never signed in.

beats._item: Jessica's, 2026-09-24 pm (office/projects/delves/testcase-01-two-halves.md, 'MESSAGE BOXES, AND THE PART GETS A NAME'), on his 'we might need message boxes as the piece missing is super vague'. They replace 'Signed-Out Consignment'. Her rule, narrowed: name the objects, never describe the site.
beats._model: His eye, 2026-09-24: the base activator wears BossContainer_Science01, an end-of-dungeon loot container, so the load read as loot. A plain stackable freight crate reads as a consignment. Eliza's pick on the placeholder-not-question rule; his to swap.

beats.journal: The filter core reached the <Place> two days ago and was taken from its crate overnight. Without it the reclaimer stays offline. I need to find whoever took it.
beats.name: Water Reclaimer
beats._name: His ask, 2026-09-24: "change the delivery point to like a machine? it's the water plant thing". The base activator is BossContainer_Science01 named 'Delivery Location'. WaterFiltrationCart01 is Eliza's placeholder pick (alternative: the LargeWaterStorage tanks); 'Water Reclaimer' is Jessica's own noun for the job.
beats.say: That's the housing, but the core's gone. Someone opened the crate in the night. We need it back, or we're drinking recycled for another week.

beats.journal: I've recovered the filter core, still sealed. I should take it back to the <Place> and get the reclaimer running.

message.title: Reclaimer Filter Core
message.text: The filter core, still sealed. Whoever took it never worked out what it was for.

beats._item: Jessica's, 2026-09-24 pm (office/projects/delves/testcase-01-two-halves.md, 'MESSAGE BOXES, AND THE PART GETS A NAME'), on his 'we might need message boxes as the piece missing is super vague'. They replace 'Signed-Out Consignment'. Her rule, narrowed: name the objects, never describe the site.

beats.journal: A water reclaimer bound for the <Place> was shipped in two crates, and neither reached it whole. I found the lost housing, recovered the stolen filter core and got the reclaimer running.
beats.say: Water's in the line. First clean water in a week. Thank you.

_messages: Texts are Jessica's, verbatim, 2026-09-24 pm. TITLES ARE ELIZA'S PLACEHOLDERS, taken from the opening words of each text: hers to rule on. Each box is a MESG cloned from duo_alocal01_msg03 with OwnerQuest set to this quest, so <Place> resolves.
_journal: Journal lines rewritten 2026-09-26 (Jessica) to vanilla's measured shape: first person, what just happened then what next, ~23 words. Beat 4 now carries the completion RECAP, which vanilla ends every quest with. Message box texts unchanged: he played them, 'It's good'. Box 4 title is Jessica's post-play ruling, Reclaimer Online.
_speech: Jessica 2026-10-09, his "setup all the json so Eliza can build it". Lines and casting: home-office office/projects/delves/radio-lines.md. No names, no places (his rulings). Only Roger is heard in game; the other voices are cast off ElevenLabs' labels, his ear decides. His "either or" 2026-10-09: a beat carries a spoken line OR a message box, never both; the spoken beats lost their boxes.
